inputChanges.before: The capability is workspace-scoped and exists from createKernel(); its members, in the object literal order; the slice holds only disabledCategories.
inputChanges.after: The capability is workspace-scoped and exists from createKernel(); its members, in the object literal order; commands live in settings and a closure registry, with no session slice.

mappings.name: icon-accent

inputChanges.before: iconAccent carries what the derivation returns: both colours, one, an empty object; null and undefined mean no accent; a throw means no accent; an absent derivation is never called.
inputChanges.after: iconAccent carries what the derivation returns: both colours or one; empty, null and undefined mean no accent; a throw means no accent; an absent derivation is never called.

mappings.partialRetirement: Empty accent object now resolves as absent since both channels are undefined; preserve literal success for both/individual colors and no accent for empty/null/undefined/throw.

mappings.name: categories

inputChanges.before: config.disabledCategories seeds the slice (copied); a command in a disabled category is disabled and hidden though its derivations still run; disable, enable and set dispatch every time, and the reducer ignores what changes nothing; execute refuses a hidden command.
inputChanges.after: config.disabledCategories seeds settings; a disabled category hides and disables its command without invoking enabled/visible; idempotent changes fire nothing; execute refuses a hidden command.

mappings.partialRetirement: No old reducer dispatch/state-change stream exists. Settings are the live owner; turned-off definitions short-circuit enabled/visible derivations, and idempotent setting changes emit nothing.

mappings.name: i18n-labels

inputChanges.before: With i18n present the label is t(labelKey), following the locale; a missing key comes back as the key (and i18n warns once); search matches the translated label.
inputChanges.after: With i18n present the label resolves the command id then labelKey through current and fallback locale; a missing key falls back to the command id and warns once; search matches the translated label.

mappings.partialRetirement: Current i18n missing-key fallback is the command id, not labelKey, while explicit labelKey translation and fallback-language translation survive.

mappings.name: command-ctx

inputChanges.before: What a command function can do with its CommandCtx: get resolves a document-scoped token for the target document and throws the kernel's refusal when it cannot; tryGet answers null instead; workspace tokens resolve whatever the target; an empty target falls back to the active document; core() is the kernel's core state.
inputChanges.after: What a command function can do with its CommandCtx: get resolves a document-scoped token for the target document and throws the kernel's refusal when it cannot; tryGet answers null instead; workspace tokens resolve whatever the target; an empty target falls back to the active document; documentId and the Documents capability expose the current document and list.

mappings.partialRetirement: Retire core() and lazy capabilityThrows: current CommandContext has documentId/get/tryGet/args/signal, and capabilities are created transactionally before document publication. Use actual DocumentsToken.list for document order, current available capability and explicit missing/no-document/loading refusals. Add bound-scope success and explicit target override steps. Opaque null context argument is replaced by omission in derivations.

mappings.name: register-many-shortcuts-and-can-execute
mappings.partialRetirement: A runtime replacement shadows configured commands. Disposing the replacement reveals the configured definition rather than deleting it. Old replacer cannot remove a newer owner.

mappings.name: a-bad-config-refuses-the-kernel

inputChanges.before: config.commands are registered when the controller is created, so a duplicate id makes createKernel throw the conflict.
inputChanges.after: Configured duplicate ids resolve to the last definition in the first insertion position; runtime registration still refuses duplicates.

mappings.partialRetirement: Configured duplicates no longer refuse construction: configuredCommands uses Map.set and the later definition wins. Preserve original name as historical key and assert current configured registration success, with independent duplicate runtime conflicts elsewhere.

mappings.name: a-bad-config-shortcut-refuses-the-kernel

inputChanges.before: An unparsable shortcut in config.commands makes createKernel throw the parse error.
inputChanges.after: An unparsable shortcut in config.commands makes the first configured-registry read throw the parse error.

mappings.partialRetirement: Shortcut validation is lazy at configured-registry access; the first listCommandIds step throws the actual parser error instead of a kernel construction refusal.

mappings.name: after-destroy

inputChanges.before: A capability reference kept past destroy still reads and changes the registry, matches strokes, resolves and executes against the last state (i18n no longer resolves, so labels are their keys); category intents are dropped, and the first is reported instance-closed.
inputChanges.after: Retained registrations and definition-only reads survive teardown; operations resolving the active document refuse through the destroyed kernel. Settings writes are dropped, and removers retain their registration identity.

mappings.partialRetirement: Old member-order refs are replaced with current actual returned function identities. Definition-only reads, registrations and removers survive; active-document lookups now refuse through kernel guardUsable, and disposed settings updates do nothing without reports.
